name: 2094.jpg
texts:
[
  "ROAD SAFETY STARTS WITH YOU",
  "Every trip. Every time.",
  "1.19 million people die on the roads each year worldwide. Most crashes are preventable.",
  "Slow down. Buckle up. Phone down. Sober up. Look twice.",
  "For drivers:
• Obey the speed limit—slow even more in school zones and neighborhoods.
• Always wear your seat belt and make sure every passenger buckles up.
• Never drive impaired by alcohol, drugs, or fatigue.
• Put the phone away—no texting, scrolling, or handheld calls while driving.
• Signal early, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield to people walking and biking.",
  "For riders and motorcyclists:
• Wear a certified, properly fastened helmet and protective gear.
• Be visible—use lights, reflective clothing, and ride predictably.
• Keep a safe following distance and avoid weaving between lanes.
• Ride sober. If you’re tired, take a break.",
  "For people walking and cycling:
• Make eye contact with drivers before crossing; don’t assume you’ve been seen.
• Use crosswalks and signals where available; look left-right-left.
• Keep headphones low and phones away near traffic.
• At night, use lights and reflective gear.",
  "For parents and caregivers:
• Use the right child car seat or booster for age and size—install it correctly.
• Children under 12 are safest in the back seat.
• Be a role model: buckle up, obey speed limits, and avoid distractions.",
  "Vehicle ready, mind ready:
• Check tires, brakes, lights, and wipers.
• Clean windshields and cameras; fix safety recalls promptly.
• Plan your route and give yourself extra time—rushing risks lives.",
  "See something unsafe? Say something.
• Report hazards like broken signals, dangerous potholes, or missing signs to local authorities.",
  "Emergency: call your local number (e.g., 112 / 911 / 999).",
  "Learn more and take the pledge: who.int/roadsafety",
  "Arrive alive. Someone is waiting for you."
]

texts:
[
  "STOP BULLYING. START BELONGING.",
  "Everyone deserves to feel safe, included, and respected - online and offline.",
  "What is bullying? Repeated, intentional behavior that hurts, humiliates, or excludes someone. It can be verbal, physical, social, or digital (cyberbullying).",
  "Harassment based on race, ethnicity, religion, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, or appearance is never okay.",
  "Bullying can look like: name-calling, threats, spreading rumors, sharing private images without consent, unwanted touching, deliberate exclusion, impersonation or doxxing, and repeated online harassment.",
  "Bullying harms mental health, attendance, and learning. We all lose when we ignore it.",
  "If you are being bullied: 1) You are not alone. 2) Stay safe - walk away when possible. 3) Save evidence (screenshots, messages). 4) Tell someone you trust (friend, parent/guardian, teacher, counselor, HR). 5) Report it using the link or QR code below. 6) Block and report online abuse. 7) Keep a dated record of what happened.",
  "If you see bullying, be an upstander: Direct (speak up if safe), Distract (shift attention, invite the person to leave with you), Delegate (get help from an adult/authority), Delay (check in and support afterward).",
  "If you have hurt someone: take responsibility, stop the behavior, apologize without excuses, ask how to repair harm, and get support to change.",
  "Words you can use in the moment: \"That's not okay.\" \"Let's keep it respectful.\" \"Are you alright? Want to walk with me?\"",
  "Reporting is safe and important. Scan the QR code or visit: [insert your reporting link]. Reports can be anonymous. Retaliation is not allowed.",
  "Need to talk? Reach out to a counselor, trusted adult, or peer support. If you are in immediate danger, call your local emergency number.",
  "Crisis support if you feel overwhelmed or unsafe: contact your local crisis line (for example, 988 in the U.S.; 116 123 in many EU countries; 1737 in New Zealand) or visit a crisis support website.",
  "Our community standard: We challenge harmful behavior, celebrate differences, and protect one another.",
  "Respect looks like: listening, using names and pronouns correctly, asking not assuming, including others, and shutting down rumors and hate.",
  "Take the pledge: I will be kind, brave, and speak up.",
  "Speak up. Report. Support. Repeat.",
  "#NoBullying #ChooseKindness #BeAnUpstander"
]

  "Use less. Waste none.",
  "Why it matters",

  "Agriculture uses about 70% of global freshwater withdrawals.",
  "What you can do",

  "Run full loads in dishwashers and washing machines.",
  "Choose water-efficient fixtures and appliances (look for efficiency labels).",
  "Replace lawns with native, drought-tolerant plants; water early in the morning.",
  "Sweep, don't hose, driveways and sidewalks.",
  "Collect rainwater where permitted; reuse graywater safely.",
  "Eat lower on the food chain more often and reduce food waste.",
  "Report broken sprinklers and water main leaks in your community.",
  "Keep paint, oil, and chemicals out of drains to protect local waters.",
  "Set a goal: reduce your daily use by 20% and track your progress.",
  "Together we can secure water for people, farms, nature, and future generations.",
  "Learn more: unwater.org • water.org • your local water utility",
  "#WaterConservation #EveryDropCounts"
]
